correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the uniform quartic support-plane gap, including the 1/12 coefficient, and the polar angle bound O(R^(-1/4)) after lattice-cell comparison; the integrable radial density has tail R^(3/4-p). Splitting the exponential gap by the supporting functional reduces the convolution quotient to two such tilted sums. Conversely the axial integers |l|<=j^(3/4), 1<=j<=N/2, give the lower bound sum j^(3/4-p). For the critical constant put D_j(l)=(j^4+l^4)^(1/4)-j for j>=0. For j>=1, D_j(l) is bounded below by a positive constant times l^4/j^3 for |l|<=j and by a constant times |l| for |l|>=j; the latter is needed for the very far tails, where a global quartic lower bound would be false. On l=j^(3/4)y, D_j(l) tends to y^4/4 uniformly on compact y-sets, and the two-regime bound supplies an integrable tail envelope for the lattice Riemann sum. The limiting endpoint mass per harmonic j-term is Gamma(1/4)/(sqrt(2)*a^(1/4)). For j<=epsilon*N and |l|<=K*j^(3/4) the long-leg defect is O(K^4*(epsilon/(1-epsilon))^3), and the long-leg polynomial quotient is bounded globally by (1-epsilon)^(-7/4); truncation followed by epsilon->0 is justified. Reflection doubles the coefficient. On the fixed interior the transverse sum is O(N^(3/4)) and the polynomial factor is O_epsilon(N^(-7/4)); outside [0,N] the extra outward gap 2*dist(j,[0,N]) makes the transverse contributions summable. The analytic argument proves all a>0 and p>=0; Fourier Cauchy–Schwarz gives sufficiency and no necessity claim about multiplication. Independent replay: python3 /workspace/review_evidence.py, lattice section. Its finite rectangles at a=2 are only scaling diagnostics, not rigorous tails or an asymptotic certificate.
